items.summary: Only the stacking curve moved: one source of anti-heal is exactly as strong, so nobody's single purchase decision changes. But the second-through-fourth sources pay less (4-stack ceiling 82.2%->72%), which quietly reverses part of the 10-30 'anti-heal is a team coverage plan' move and restores relative value to kit-based sustain.

affected_heroes.why: Healbane is his answer to sustain comps; the payoff for adding it on top of a teammate's heal-cut is now materially smaller, so his counter-build is less of a hard counter.

His Toxic Bullets 40% heal-cut plus Healbane is exactly the two-source case trimmed 57.8%->54.7%, but the same change leaves his Spirit Lifesteal/Napalm sustain less punished by enemy stacked anti-heal — roughly a wash.
The anti-heal bruiser variant's whole selling point was built-in heal cut stacking with Healbane/Toxic Bullets; that composition is the nerfed case, so his edge into healer comps shrinks.
He still buys Healbane for self/team anti-heal, but the dome and Healing Booster throughput he sells is now harder for a team to fully shut down with multiple anti-heal sources.
The 10-30 stack system was the worst change for her tether heals; capping the stack ceiling partially un-does that, though her gun core remains the correct build.
He buys Healbane himself, but more importantly his post-10-30 problem was starting fights small — a weaker anti-heal ceiling on his regen stack buys back some of the buffer Radiant Regeneration lost.
Scorn sustain is his survive-the-fight engine; less effective stacked anti-heal on him is the one item-side gain for a tank whose spirit damage was gutted on 10-30.
Restorative Locket carries his sustain after Healing Booster was gutted, and that heal is now harder to fully suppress with stacked anti-heal.

items.build_shift: No component or slot change — it stays a Vitality T2 — but its marginal value collapses for a team's second and third buyer, so on a comp that already has one Healbane the slot now competes with any other Vitality item instead of reading as free coverage.

notable_item_stories: Anti-heal is back to being a slot you buy rather than a coverage plan you draft: single-source Healbane is untouched, so expect fewer triple-Healbane comps and a small rebound for kit healers (Kelvin, Ivy) and self-sustain bruisers (Shiv, Mo & Krill).

The losers are the heroes who used Healbane as a second layer over their own heal-cut (Infernus with Toxic Bullets, Drifter's built-in cut, Seven into sustain comps) — that specific stack is now worth about 3 points less at two sources and far less at four.
